one_line: Vaishnavite reformer-king of 18th‑century Manipur who reshaped Kangleipak’s polity, faith and identity.

appearance.age_look: Early 40s, athletic and wiry, with the poised bearing of a seasoned warrior-king.
appearance.face: Oval face with high cheekbones, warm medium-brown complexion, straight nose, sharp jawline, slightly arched brows and intense, focused eyes; a faint vertical worry line between the brows; default expression calm but steely, often with a hint of determined resolve.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair pulled tightly into a high topknot at the back of the crown, smoothed at the sides, with a simple narrow white cloth band tied around the base of the knot and a small tilak at the center of the forehead.
appearance.costume: He wears an 18th‑century Manipuri royal outfit: a knee‑length white cotton dhoti wrapped tightly and pleated to the front, bordered with a thin red stripe; a fitted, long‑sleeved, hip‑length pale cream angarkha-style upper garment overlapping and tied to the right, with subtle off‑white woven texture; over this a saffron‑orange silk uttariya scarf draped from the left shoulder across the torso and around the back; simple dark brown leather sandals; jewellery limited to a narrow gold necklace close to the neck, a single thin gold armlet on the right upper arm with a small conch motif, and small gold ear studs; no fantastical armor, only a plain dark red cloth waistband that subtly suggests courtly status.
appearance.signature: A long, slightly curved steel tulwar with a simple brass hilt and a plain, unadorned scabbard of dark brown leather, worn at his left hip and often held in his right hand as he stands in a commanding yet measured pose.

ref_desc: King Pamheiba Gharib Niwaz is a wiry, medium-brown, sharp-featured man in his early 40s with a black topknot and white headband, wearing a white dhoti, cream angarkha, saffron scarf, minimal gold jewellery, and carrying a curved steel tulwar in a dark brown scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of King Pamheiba Gharib Niwaz: an 18th‑century Manipuri warrior-king in his early 40s, wiry and athletic, with an oval, sharp-featured face, medium-brown skin, intense focused eyes and a calm but steely expression, a faint vertical line between his brows, and thick black hair pulled into a high topknot tied with a narrow white cloth band and a small tilak on his forehead; dress him in a historically grounded Manipuri royal costume with a tightly wrapped knee-length white cotton dhoti bordered by a thin red stripe, a fitted long-sleeved pale cream angarkha-style upper garment overlapping and tied to the right with subtle off-white woven texture, and a saffron-orange silk uttariya scarf draped from his left shoulder across his torso and around his back; add a plain dark red cloth waistband, simple dark brown leather sandals, a narrow gold necklace, a single thin gold armlet with a small conch motif on his right upper arm, and small gold ear studs; at his left hip show a long slightly curved steel tulwar with a simple brass hilt in a plain dark brown leather scabbard, and in some views have him holding the tulwar in his right hand in a composed, authoritative stance; ensure the dominant colours are white, cream, saffron orange, dark red and dark brown, and present multiple angles to clearly show his consistent face, hair, costume and weapon details.
